followups.problem: Followup (a) remains: boardAnswers probes the token-free /api/health and accepts any {ok:true, version:string} body, so the token in the URL it prints (identity token at line 480, board.json token at line 469) is never checked against the running server.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Another watch server on the identity port, for example a manual `swarm watch --all --keep-up --port 51058` run after the identity file was replaced, or any local service whose /api/health returns that shape, makes `swarm watch --all` exit 0 and print or open a link that returns 401. No second board starts, so the user has no working board until they kill the other process. This is a dead link, not data exposure, because the probe sends no token.
followups.fix: After the health probe passes, send one token-bearing check with the token in a header and redirect:'manual', for example a HEAD or light /api/board call. Alternatively, have /api/health return a non-secret token fingerprint (such as the first 8 hex characters of sha256(token)) and compare it before reusing the board.

followups.problem: Followup (b) remains: the launchd path confirms success only by the version answering at record.port. pollNewVersion returns body.pid, but nothing checks it against the pid that launchctl reports after the kickstart.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Low risk. If the kickstarted job fails to bind and a different targetVersion board (for example one started by hand) takes the same port during the poll window, the result is restarted-launchd while the launchd job is crash-looping.
followups.fix: After confirm.ok, run `launchctl print` again and require that its pid equals confirm.pid (when the health body includes a pid). Otherwise report 'failed' with the kickstart hint.

followups.problem: Followup (c) is partly addressed. The busy-port skip now requires !loaded, so a stray board falls through to the normal path whenever the job is loaded. When the job is not loaded, though, every old-version board record or discovered board on a busy port is still treated as the launchd board. Nothing checks identity.port === record.port first.
followups.exploit_or_failure: With the plist installed but the job booted out, a manual or background board on some other port (not the keep-up port) gets status launchd-not-loaded and a bootstrap hint. It is never restarted, so it keeps serving the old version. The failure is safe (no kill, no spawn) but the guidance is misleading.
followups.fix: Gate the skip on the same owner match: `!loaded && available && identity && identity.port === record.port && !(await defaultIsPortFree(record.port))`. Any other board then falls through to the manual or terminal path. Add a test with an unloaded job and a held stray port, expecting status 'restarted'.

followups.problem: The 1.167.34 entry still says '55 focused tests' and does not mention the owner match. The evidence after the fix records 54 focused tests, and the launchd bullet at line 12 does not say kickstart now applies only to the board matching the keep-up port or launchd pid, at most once per update.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Release notes are inaccurate. No runtime effect.
followups.fix: Change the count to 54 and add to the launchd bullet: 'only for the board on the keep-up port or launchd pid, at most once per update; other boards keep the manual/terminal path'.

summary: The delta review confirms the blocker is fixed. The keep-up identity is read once per call (server-restart.mjs:821), and the launchd pid is parsed from `launchctl print` (909-912). The kickstart branch runs only when loaded && (identity.port === record.port || launchdPid === record.pid) (917). A per-call launchdKicked guard allows at most one kickstart and skips later launchd items without signal or spawn (886, 918, 921), and it is set before the kickstart, so a failed kickstart also blocks duplicates. A stray board on another port with a loaded job now reaches the existing pid-probe, terminal and manual path (942 onward). Each scenario is covered by tests: tests/one-board-owner.test.mjs:341-358 (stray background or terminal board, zero kickstarts), :360-366 (stale pid with matching port, one kickstart), :368-375 (registry plus discovery, one kickstart, no signal or spawn), plus the existing launchd, unloaded-job, fallback and kickstart-failure tests. On the earlier followups: (a) the health probe still does not validate the printed token, so it remains a followup; (b) success is still confirmed by version alone, a low-risk followup; (c) the busy-port skip is fixed for a loaded job, but with an unloaded job it still catches stray boards (a safe failure, but the hint is misleading), so it remains a followup. The watch --all reuse path (watch-cli.mjs:1036-1043) is unchanged since the first review: it runs after the --json, --text/--tui and --keep-up branches, reads the identity without writing it, falls back to board.json with a live-pid check, and starts one board otherwise. The open and fetch injections are behavior-neutral. I found no regressions in the rest of the diff (version pins and release tests are consistent at 1.167.34). Limits: this review is based only on reading the listed files. I ran nothing, and the suite results (7672 tests, 7641 pass, 0 fail; focused 54/54) come from the evidence file. discoverRunningServers was not in my context, so I assumed a discovered record's .port is the numeric listen port, as the registry-plus-discovery test implies.
